turns.user: I need published mortars with drying shrinkage no more than 600 microstrain at 28 days and compressive strength of at least 50 MPa.
turns.text:
I’ll search the literature records for mortars that meet both reported 28-day thresholds, then check the source details and units.
The literature search labels several results “exact,” but its preview includes records without both 28-day measurements. I’ll check the underlying database so the shortlist uses measured values at the requested age.
I found five mortar records with both requested measurements at 28 days. I’m checking their mix ingredients and test methods before listing them.
The literature database has **five mortar records** with both a 28-day shrinkage entry at or below 600 microstrain and a 28-day compressive strength of at least 50 MPa. These are reported measurements, not model predictions.

| Published mix | 28-day shrinkage (microstrain) | 28-day strength (MPa) | Mix details |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| [EX-S-L-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2017.12.001) | 129 | 65 | Portland/CSA cement 85/15; shrinkage reducing admixture; 20% lightweight fine aggregate; w/b 0.40 |
| [EX-S-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2017.12.001) | 192 | 63 | Portland/CSA cement 85/15; shrinkage reducing admixture; w/b 0.40 |
| [CA120](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2024.111672) | 203 | 89 | Portland and calcium aluminate cements, fly ash, silica fume and steel fibre; w/b 0.18 |
| [J3](https://doi.org/10.1155/2017/6384859) | 411 | 109.4 | Portland cement, silica fume, silica sand and shrinkage reducing admixture; reported w/b 0.20 |
| [GOS50](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2024.109833) | 574 | 120.03 | Portland cement, silica fume, glass and oyster shell powders, sand and steel fibre; w/b 0.18 |

**Check before selecting a mix:** EX-S-L-6 and EX-S-6 are reported as *drying deformation*; the database notes that the paper’s sign convention treats positive deformation as expansion. CA120’s paper appears to have a shrinkage-unit typo, which the database interpreted as microstrain. The compression specimen groups also differ across papers. None of these records is from a 3D printing study, so printability remains unverified.

The database exported the [matching records](<C:\Users\User\3D Printing Concrete Prediction\artifacts\reports\agent\20261016-172309-463e\sql_1792139014.csv>), [mix components](<C:\Users\User\3D Printing Concrete Prediction\artifacts\reports\agent\20261016-172309-463e\sql_1792139024.csv>), [test details](<C:\Users\User\3D Printing Concrete Prediction\artifacts\reports\agent\20261016-172309-463e\sql_1792139030.csv>), and [original-value checks](<C:\Users\User\3D Printing Concrete Prediction\artifacts\reports\agent\20261016-172309-463e\sql_1792139034.csv>).

input.sql: SELECT p.doi,p.title,p.year,p.is_3dcp_study,m.mix_uid,m.mix_id,m.name_in_paper,m.w_b_reported,m.sand_binder_ratio,m.curing_regime,CAST(s.value_canonical AS REAL) AS shrinkage_microstrain,CAST(c.value_canonical AS REAL) AS strength_MPa,s.value_kind AS shrinkage_kind,s.fig_only AS shrinkage_fig_only,s.source_locator AS shrinkage_source,c.value_kind AS strength_kind,c.fig_only AS strength_fig_only,c.source_locator AS strength_source,ts.comparability_group AS shrinkage_group,tc.comparability_group AS strength_group FROM mixes m JOIN papers p ON p.paper_uid=m.paper_uid JOIN measurements s ON s.mix_uid=m.mix_uid JOIN measurements c ON c.mix_uid=m.mix_uid LEFT JOIN tests ts ON ts.test_uid=s.test_uid LEFT JOIN tests tc ON tc.test_uid=c.test_uid WHERE m.system_type='mortar' AND s.quantity='drying_shrinkage' AND c.quantity='compressive_strength' AND s.age_norm_d!='' AND c.age_norm_d!='' AND CAST(s.age_norm_d AS REAL)=28 AND CAST(c.age_norm_d AS REAL)=28 AND s.value_canonical!='' AND c.value_canonical!='' AND s.unit_canonical='microstrain' AND c.unit_canonical='MPa' AND CAST(s.value_canonical AS REAL)>=0 AND CAST(s.value_canonical AS REAL)<=600 AND CAST(c.value_canonical AS REAL)>=50 ORDER BY CAST(s.value_canonical AS REAL),CAST(c.value_canonical AS REAL) DESC LIMIT 200
